Former heavyweight contender, Dillian Whyte, has predicted that the fight between British-Nigerian, Anthony Joshua, and Tyson Fury will end in an early knockout, and says it may not last beyond the first round. Whyte, who has fought both men, told Sky Sports Boxing that he would be surprised if the contest on December 11 went beyond five rounds. The fight takes place at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, with three heavyweight bouts confirmed for the undercard. He said the rivals had changed since the fight was first talked about six years ago. “It might be an even better fight now than it would have been. Six years ago, the guys were more cagey; they had better defence, better feet. If you asked me six years ago, I would have said either AJ by KO or Fury by points,” he said. “Now, they are both showing vulnerability. Fury could knock him out in a round. AJ could knock out Fury in a round.” Fury blames Joshua for mega-fight delays Okolie predicts Joshua knockout win over Fury I’ll bring more than power to Fury fight – Joshua He added that Fury’s speed had dropped, saying, “Tyson’s feet have slowed down; he is not as fast as he was, not as reactive as he was. AJ has shown a lot of vulnerability, and he has been through a lot of things, mentally, as well. So, I think that it is going to be a great fight. I would be surprised if it lasts five rounds.” Whyte beat Joshua as an amateur, but was stopped by him in 2015 when they fought for the British title. Joshua went on to win a world title in his next fight. Whyte’s first world title challenge came against Fury in 2022, when he was knocked out as the Briton defended his belt at home for the first time in his career.
